The closing identity $\prod_{j=2}^n(1-1/j)=1/n$ matches the unsquared recursion, confirming the factors were dropped. issues.failure_explanation: (i) Lemma a18's first hypothesis forces $s\ge s_{\min}=\frac{2^{3(K+1)}\eps^2n^2R^{2K}}{\rho^K}$, so Lemma a16's contribution is at least $\binom n{m+1}s_{\min}^{m+1}$, which is larger than the claimed $n^{m+3}R^{2K(m+1)}\eps^{2(m+1)}$ by a factor $\ge\frac{2^{3(K+1)(m+1)}n^{m-1}}{(m+1)!\,\rho^{K(m+1)}}\ge 2^{9}\rho^{-K}$-ish; already at $\rho\le1$ this is $\ge512$, so the claimed $\eps^{2(m+1)}$ coefficient is unattainable through these lemmas. (ii) In the polylogarithmic-sparsity regime the paper advertises ($n\rho=O(\log^2 n)$, e.g. $\rho=\Theta(\log^2n/n)$, $K=\frac{2\log n}{\log(n\rho)}$), substituting $s_{\min}$ into Lemma a18's second hypothesis gives a left side $\asymp 6K\log(n)\cdot n^{-K/(K+1)}\gg\rho$ (numerically, LHS$/\rho\approx5\cdot10^3$ at $\rho=\log^2n/n$), so the two hypotheses are jointly unsatisfiable, Lemma a18 is vacuous there, and the Comp-case bound cannot be obtained. (iii) Even where feasible, Lemma a18 delivers the additive term $e^{-n\rho/2}$, not the claimed $e^{-\rho n}$. Hence Proposition a19 is unsupported as stated.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: All of our results hold if complex Gaussians are replaced by any sufficiently concentrated absolutely continuous distribution on $\C$

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract, \eqref{a5}, Remark \ref{a26} ('All of our results hold if complex Gaussians are replaced by any sufficiently concentrated absolutely continuous distribution') and the table row 'This work' advertise the polylogarithmic guarantees at sparsity $\rho=O(\log^2 n/n)$. These are proved only through Proposition \ref{a19}, whose proof requires Lemma \ref{a18}'s two hypotheses simultaneously; in this regime those hypotheses are jointly unsatisfiable (evaluating the second at the forced $s=s_{\min}$ gives LHS $\asymp 6K\log(n)\,n^{-K/(K+1)}\gg\rho$, e.g. a factor $\approx5\cdot10^3$ too large at $n=e^{100}$, $\rho=\log^2n/n$). What the paper establishes is, at most, the sparse-regime bounds in regimes where Lemma \ref{a18} applies (roughly $n\rho\gtrsim n^{\alpha}$); the polylogarithmic conclusion for $O(n\log^2 n)$ perturbations is claimed but not established.
